expectations.text: Treats the request as wanting to be taught: the outline or first message makes clear that it will explain first and check after each part
expectations.evidence: "我每次只讲一小块，讲完马上请你做一道小题"; each outline line starts with 先讲 / 先看 … 再…

expectations.text: Does not open by quizzing the learner on decorators themselves (a single starting-point question on a prerequisite such as functions is acceptable)
expectations.evidence: No content question at all; only setup questions.

expectations.text: Says, in about one sentence, that the outline or explanations come from general knowledge rather than the learner's course or material
expectations.evidence: "下面的内容来自通用知识，以 Python 3 为准，不是照某本教材讲的。"

expectations.text: Asks at most the necessary setup questions (e.g. time) in one message, or starts with one chunk and one check; never two open questions about the content
expectations.evidence: All setup questions are in one message and none is about the content, but it asks four (a–d). b) and c) follow the teach-route template; d) "你手边能运行 Python 吗？" is not necessary before starting. Strict reading: fail.

expectations.text: Does not produce a long lecture covering several points

notes: Teach route chosen from the wording 教我 alone, which is the new routing rule.
